title: Acceleration Whiplash — Empirical Evidence for Harness Engineering
source: LIDR Harness Engineering Workshop (Sep 2026), Álvaro Moya
summary: Industry-scale empirical data proving that ungovernered AI-assisted development increases individual throughput while simultaneously degrading team quality metrics. This evidence is the empirical foundation for EOS Harness Engineering, Tripartite Pre-Merge Evaluation, and Evidence Over Claims policies.

adoption_scale.ai_assistant_usage: 92.6% of developers use AI assistants monthly (Stack Overflow 2025)
adoption_scale.salary_premium: +28% average salary (~$18,000 USD/year) for developers with AI skills (Lightcast)

perception_vs_reality.finding: Developers without structured systems completed tasks 19% SLOWER with AI while believing they were 20% FASTER
perception_vs_reality.implication: Subjective velocity perception is unreliable; only deterministic sensor output (tests, linters, exit codes) provides valid evidence

eos_policy_mapping.tripartite_pre_merge: Directly addresses 31.3% unreviewed PRs and +441% review time — automated sensor gates replace manual bottleneck
eos_policy_mapping.evidence_over_claims: Directly addresses METR perception gap — agents cannot self-certify velocity or quality
eos_policy_mapping.harness_engineering: Directly addresses +54% bugs and +242.7% incidents — structured harness with guides and sensors prevents quality degradation
eos_policy_mapping.tool_pruning: Indirectly addresses throughput gains — focused tool exposure maximizes quality of AI output while maintaining speed
